recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the published clarification in current core datatype build inputs without changing conformance semantics or the separate guidance about actual time zone codes.
issue_request: FHIR-24564 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core datatypes and requested replacing primitive datatype references to time zones with UTC offsets because +zz:zz represents an offset from UTC rather than a named time zone.
initial_application: The R5 MnM batch commit 5cbc14c7d0f361941099bf72066b75c3f74f6d4f explicitly listed FHIR-24564 and changed source/datatypes/primitives.xml from time-zone wording to UTC-offset wording. It did not update all parallel datatype narrative/example source, and later edits left source/datatypes.html and source/datatypes-examples.html with timezone-offset wording.
additional_context: The linked Zulip #implementers thread confirms the rationale: dateTime values carry offsets, while true named time-zone codes remain a separate concept handled by the timezone extension. Current source/datatypes/primitives.xml already uses UTC offset, so the safe reconciliation was to align source/datatypes.html and source/datatypes-examples.html while preserving true time-zone-code references.
reconciliation: Changed source/datatypes.html for date, dateTime, instant, and time from timezone-offset wording to UTC offset, and changed both XML and JSON instant examples in source/datatypes-examples.html from including timezone to including a UTC offset.
source_changes: source/datatypes.html: date, dateTime, instant, and time primitive rows now say UTC offset where the lexical value constrains an offset.
source/datatypes-examples.html: XML and JSON instant examples now describe +01:00 as a UTC offset rather than a timezone.
